bridge: software verification -> audit-first deterministic reference kernel
novelty_signal: This is the strongest surviving wedge because it differentiates the project from REBOUND, poliastro, PhET, and hobby demos by centering analytic controls, invariant logging, timestep convergence, and replay fingerprints rather than UI, speed, or a new integrator.
validation_plan: Run closed-form two-body checks, long-horizon conservation logs, timestep-halving convergence tables, and bounded cross-runtime replay tests on the reference scenarios.
risk: If the audit surfaces are secondary to the simulator itself, the work reads like a textbook reimplementation or a smaller REBOUND.

novelty_signal: Benchmarks show close encounters are the only regime where the direct kernel fails badly, so a deterministic queue that narrows expensive handling to that regime is more defensible than broad performance work.
validation_plan: Measure queue determinism, trigger precision on star-grazing and unequal-mass flyby scenes, and whether encounter mode materially lowers energy spikes versus the same global dt.
risk: If it behaves like an opaque heuristic or only saves runtime without improving trust, it becomes a thin TRACE-adjacent engineering tweak.

bridge: software verification -> round-trip error as runtime trust signal
novelty_signal: Using forward/backward mismatch as a machine-readable honesty signal supports the 'not just an animation' defense and is more distinctive than claiming exact reversibility.
validation_plan: Check whether round-trip error rises before visible failure and correlates with REBOUND deviation and invariant drift across all published scenes.
risk: If the signal is only descriptive and not predictive or actionable, it reduces to a debugging metric with weak novelty.

novelty_signal: Offline calibration may keep the runtime small and reduce ad hoc hand-tuning, but it is only interesting if named presets remain stable on held-out scenes and stay transparent.
validation_plan: Fit softening and encounter thresholds on teacher traces, then test whether fast, stable, and teaching presets preserve their ranking on unseen cases.
risk: High overfitting risk; hidden knobs would undermine the honesty story.

bridge: computer graphics -> resolution-coupled softening and projection layer
novelty_signal: This could become an honesty layer for unresolved scales, but current feedback does not show that it solves the benchmark failure better than encounter-specific handling.
validation_plan: Quantify projection magnitude, softening sensitivity, and whether drift improves without masking real close-encounter physics.
risk: It can easily look like bad-physics camouflage or an unprincipled graphics hack.

bridge: large-N acceleration -> neighbor trees, event-sparse far field, and patch streaming
novelty_signal: Weak. Barnes-Hut, REBOUND, and many existing demos already occupy the fast-gravity branch, so this does not improve the novelty case.
validation_plan: Keep only as a non-headline engineering branch and reject it if the main win is speed on small N.
risk: High risk of turning the project into a small-REBOUND clone or performance paper.

bridge: education/product packaging -> classroom or web sandbox framing
novelty_signal: Weak. PhET, Universe Sandbox, and hobby repositories already dominate the classroom and web-sandbox framing.
validation_plan: Only revive if a separate study shows measurable trust or pedagogy gains from the audit outputs.
risk: A reviewer can dismiss the work as another demo immediately.

bridge: exact reversibility -> JANUS-style bitwise replay claims
novelty_signal: Weak. JANUS already owns exact bitwise reversibility, and the current probe explicitly scoped that claim out.
validation_plan: Do not pursue unless the project adopts a new exact arithmetic design, which is outside the minimal-kernel focus.
risk: It inflates scope and invites a direct JANUS comparison the project is not built to win.
